items.title: Bitcoin Technical Reversal and Price Forecast
points: Galaxy Research reversed its call that Bitcoin's bear market ended in June, after Bitcoin failed to hold above its 50-week moving average (a trend indicator averaging price over the past 50 weeks), which broke down in early November.
The firm flagged $58,525 (the June 30 low) as a critical support level — a daily close below this could signal the start of a deeper decline.
Historical precedent suggests the eventual bottom could be at least 17% lower than that level, implying potential downside to around $48,536 or below.
Bitcoin is currently trading around $60,500 after dipping to $57,308, pressured by inflation data and proposed U.S. tariffs on November 26.

items.title: Crypto Market Outflows and Regulatory Tightening
points: Spot Bitcoin ETFs (exchange-traded funds that let investors gain Bitcoin exposure through regular stock accounts) saw $5.39 billion in net outflows in November, tracking toward their worst month on record.
Standard Chartered's Zodia Custody disclosed a data breach exposing client and staff names and emails, but confirmed no unauthorized account transactions occurred.

UK's Financial Conduct Authority (FCA) plans the strictest DeFi (decentralized finance — financial services built on blockchain without traditional intermediaries) rules among major markets, requiring platform authorization and barring regulated exchanges from routing UK retail trades to unregulated DeFi platforms.

Standard Chartered's Zodia Custody disclosed hackers accessed client contact details but found no unauthorized transactions.

sections.title: Bitcoin Technical Reversal and Price Forecast

The firm identified $58,525 (the June 30 low) as a critical support level—if Bitcoin closes below this daily, it signals the start of a deeper decline.
In every comparable historical case, the eventual bottom came at least 17% lower than this level, suggesting potential downside to around $48,536 or below.
Bitcoin currently sits at $60,467, vulnerable to the breakdown threshold as macro headwinds from inflation data and proposed U.S. tariffs pressured markets on November 26.
